title: Per-tenant admission + regional soft-fallback for Redis/Kafka hotspots
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware admission controller that enforces per-tenant token-bucket admission and a soft regional fallback path for downstream hotspots (Redis and Kafka). The feature should limit noisy tenants, protect connection pools, and provide an automated degradational path that prefers local cached/stale reads or read-only replicas before tripping global circuit breakers. The controller should be SLO-driven (error budget aware) and expose controls for ops to tune buckets, backoff, and region-fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant token-bucket implemented for API fronting the Redis/KV and Kafka write paths
Adaptive token rates driven by per-tenant real-time SLO consumption metrics (per-tenant P99 latency and request error budget)
Region soft-fallback implemented: when remote region hits configured saturation, requests routed to local cache or read replica with clear telemetry tags
Connection pool exhaustion avoided in staging during a synthetic hotspot test (no outbound 5xx from downstream due to pool exhaustion)
Grafana dashboard created with per-tenant admission meters, regional fallback counts, and eviction/rejection reasons
E2E chaos test added to CI that simulates Redis overload and validates fallback behavior and rollback safety
Runbook entries created and oncall training completed (incidents reproducible in staging)
Load tests demonstrate <5% additional median latency on protected paths under normal load and <10% increased P99 during controlled shedding
steps: Design: finalize token-bucket model, time windows, and initial per-tenant default rates (Confluence: /wiki/downstream-resilience/admission-controller)
Instrumentation: add per-tenant SLO counters (error budget burn, P50/P90/P99) and expose to metrics pipeline
Implement admission controller library in runtime (go): accepts tenant_id, desired_units, checks token bucket, consults SLO store, returns admit/reject/soft-fallback decision
Integrate with Redis/KV client wrappers: consult admission before issuing commands; implement short-circuit to local cache/stale-read path
Integrate with Kafka producer path: throttled producers should be queued by local backpressure and optionally route to an ephemeral retention topic for later replay
Region fallback orchestration: implement policy service that monitors region-level saturation and updates per-node filters via config push
Automated tests: unit tests for token logic, integration tests for client wrappers, and an e2e chaos scenario in staging
Docs and runbook: publish operational dashboard and oncall playbook before canary rollout
mitigation_playbook: If widespread rejects spike: set global emergency throttle to permissive, enable immediate rollback of admission rules via config flag
If connection pools still exhaust: temporarily increase pool size for affected service, enable additional fallback replicas
If regional fallback causes data-consistency concerns: toggle fallback to read-only mode and notify product teams to pause writes
Use Grafana 'tenant-fallback-alert' to page oncall; attach 'fallback-debug' trace id for root-cause investigation
comments: 2026-01-24 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: scoped MVP to Redis KV read/write and Kafka producer write path. Agreed to prototype token-bucket in runtime layer and keep policy decisions externalized.

2026-01-27 - Marco Ruiz: Initial design PR posted. Key tradeoff: per-tenant buckets increase cardinality in metrics. Proposal: shard tenants into tiers for default rates and only materialize explicit buckets for high-usage tenants.

2026-01-29 - Design review (Lina Chen): Concern about cascading stale reads causing downstream consistency problems for stateful customers. Decision: fallback to cache is allowed only for 'best-effort' routes; write paths must queue or reject with clear error code recommending retry-algorithm.

2026-02-01 - Reliability review (David Kim): Suggested tying admission thresholds to rolling 5m error-budget burn rather than static rates. Action: add SLO adapter in step 3. Marco to prototype adapter by 2026-02-05.
2026-02-02 - QA (Priya Nair): Added e2e chaos scenarios to test matrix: Redis-Slow, Kafka-timeout, and region-blackhole. Will run during staging canary and report regressions.

2026-02-02 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented admission library skeleton and local unit tests. Pushed branch runtime/admission/mvp. CI failing on two integration tests (metrics label explosion). Investigating sharding approach. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218
